links.passage: Thermally-based techniques currently employed in evaluating water stress for automatic irrigation scheduling include crop canopy temperature, CWSI (empirical or theoretical), and time temperature threshold (O’Shaughnessy and Evett, 2010).
supporting_passages: The CWSI algorithm is mostly used for automatic irrigation control systems in order to improve crop water productivity.
links.inference_note: The cited sentence names thermally-based automatic irrigation scheduling techniques including CWSI, and the next sentence states that the CWSI algorithm is used in automatic irrigation control systems to improve crop water productivity.
links.section: Real-time irrigation scheduling with thermal UAS

links.passage: Bellvert et al. (2016) used a UAS with a thermal sensor to fly over grape vineyards and obtained water stress information for real-time irrigation scheduling.
supporting_passages: Leaf water potential obtained from the CWSI was successfully used as an irrigation trigger and there was no negative effect on yield and composition of the crop.
links.inference_note: The cited sentence names the UAS thermal sensor used for scheduling, and the following sentence states that triggering irrigation from the resulting CWSI sustained yield and crop composition.
